_comment: Audience order (Sept 2026 transcripts): WorldFish researchers first — finding what other teams built and what can be reused — then external research partners, then funders. Scope is aquatic food systems as a whole. The page reads as the front of a register: what we do → which areas → what that looks like → who built what (initiatives, each carrying its tools) → what the rest is built on → where it runs → what it changed → what is new. The order follows the schema: initiatives contain tools, so they lead; tool↔tool connections cut across initiatives, so the shared layer follows. Each section is the database rendered, not copy about it. The old 'Built once, then reused' essay is gone: the arrangement makes that argument now. A featured card's `href` names where its story belongs and `fallback` is used only while that target has nothing to show — app/page.js switches back on its own. Standing rule: publish no figure that cannot be traced to a source.

hero.headline: We build the digital systems behind decisions in aquatic food systems.
hero.subline: Most of those systems are managed with whatever data exists. Usually not much. This is everything we have built to change that — what each thing does, where it runs, and what it depends on.

featured.title: Monitoring that fisheries officers actually use
featured.description: In Zanzibar, Kenya and Mozambique the same pipeline turns vessel tracks and catch records into a current picture of fleet activity — not a retrospective one.
featured.imageAlt: Fishers and dhows in shallow water off Zanzibar at dusk

featured.title: Where small-scale fishers actually go
featured.description: Vessel GPS, self-reported catch and bathymetry combined into a picture of fishing effort that has never existed for small-scale fleets.
featured.imageAlt: Tracks map showing fishing visit frequency over coastal bathymetry

featured.title: From what is caught to what is eaten
featured.description: Catch composition carries nutrient content. Linking the two turns fisheries data into evidence for nutrition policy — including from gleaning, which most statistics miss entirely.
featured.imageAlt: Women and children gleaning on a tidal flat at low tide

sharedLayer.kicker: What the rest is built on
sharedLayer.title: The pieces that carry the others
sharedLayer.lead: Tools ranked by how many other tools are built on top of them. These are the pieces that cross initiatives — the reason a new deployment costs less than the last one, and the shortest answer to “is there already something I can use”.

showcase.title: The same system, one country at a time
showcase.lead: Each of these is the shared pipeline and API above, configured for a different fishery and run with a different national institution. Not four systems — one, four times.

results.title: Outcomes, with their evidence
results.lead: Each entry names the place, the institution we worked with, what changed, and how well that change is evidenced. Where no independent assessment exists yet, it says so.
